turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Margaret, I'll grab your blood pressure before you go in. Pop your arm out for me.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, this one? Sorry, I get flustered. My daughter's usually the one who remembers which arm.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Either's fine. That's 148 over 86, pulse 78. I'll put it on the screen for him.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 148 bad? She told me if it climbs I ought to panic. She's the one who does my webster pack, I just swallow whatever's in the little boxes.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): He'll go through it with you. In you go, he's just fighting the computer.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I nearly left the webster pack on the bus, it's the blue one in my bag. Sorry, I'm all over the shop today.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): No worries, stick it on the chair. Sorry, this screen's frozen on your medication list. What's been going on?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): My ankles are puffy, both of them, and I get short of puff just walking to the letterbox. Then I lie awake thinking it's my heart and I can't sleep for worrying.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, run that past me again, I was half reading the letter. The ankles, when did they start?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. Last winter, or the one before, I honestly can't pin it. I meant to write it on the calendar and then I just didn't.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): So we've got no real date for the swelling. The short of puff, same sort of time?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that one's newer. Maybe a few weeks. I'm not sure of the actual day. Is a few weeks bad, should I have come earlier?
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll sort the timing. Any chest pain with the puffing?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain, I keep checking. And no cough either, in case you were about to ask.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): I was, yes. Do you wake up gasping at night, or is the swelling going right up the legs?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Not gasping. It's just the ankles and a bit of the feet, worse by the arvo, shoes won't go on. If I put them up on the sofa it eases.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. And you said your daughter does the webster pack?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): She stays most nights, yes, sort of lives in. I take the water tablet in the morning, that's the frusemide, and a little white one I can never remember the name of. The cholesterol one got stopped.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Screen's jumped again. Who stopped the cholesterol tablet?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): The doctor at the hospital clinic. I can't remember the month, it was whenever that was. He stopped it because my legs were aching, and I haven't taken it since.

[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, atorvastatin, that's discontinued. On the little white one, the list has perindopril 4 mg and also Coversyl 4 mg, same medicine entered twice. Are you taking both?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know. Some mornings, well most mornings I think, there are two little white ones in the compartment. She said the hospital added one and the GP one was already there. Am I poisoning myself?
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not saying that. Repeat it for me, two white ones most days? I didn't catch it cleanly.

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Most days, I reckon. I get anxious and I tip the whole compartment in. And the water tablet doesn't match either. She wrote 20 on the lid, the letter says 20, but the actual tablets are the 40 ones.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Two stories on the frusemide dose, then. I won't lock in what you've been swallowing from that. Any allergies I should know before I change something?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing I'm allergic to. Well, actually, is the leg aching an allergy? No, he said muscles, not a rash, so no allergies.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll call it no known allergies. Both ankles are puffy and they pit when I press, calves are soft, no redness. Chest is clear, no crackles. Heart sounds are fine, no murmur I can hear today.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): So it isn't my heart? You said no crackles. What if it only comes on at night, when you can't hear it?

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to conclude heart failure from this. Thinking out loud, the swelling could be the veins, could be the salt and the water tablet being muddled, could still be a bit of fluid from the heart, and I'm not picking one yet.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): So which one is it? Do I need a scan? My sister had a clot, shouldn't you check me for that?
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your sister's clot isn't your diagnosis. No chest pain, calves are soft, I'm not chasing a clot today. I do want bloods, kidney function and a BNP, so we can see.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): What's a BNP? Will it hurt? And if you change the tablets my daughter will have a fit, she spent all Sunday on that pack.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): A BNP just hints at strain on the heart, it isn't a diagnosis on its own. I am changing one medicine: stop both white tablets, perindopril 4 mg one only in the morning, and Coversyl comes off because it's the same drug.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): One perindopril in the morning, not two. And the water tablet, do I take the 20 or the 40? I don't want to guess.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll set frusemide at 40 mg once each morning, one tablet. If an old compartment still has an extra, don't swallow a second.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Forty, once, no extras. What if the swelling doesn't budge? Do I come back here or go to the hospital? I always think I should go to the hospital.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the swelling is settling, see me in two weeks and bring the webster pack. If you're suddenly gasping, or you get chest pain, that's an emergency, you don't wait for me.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, and bring the pack. Is the blood test today?
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Today, yes. Kidney function and the BNP. I'll also send a note so the pack is corrected, one perindopril and frusemide 40.
[SEG0040] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I've got the form printed, Margaret. Pathology's just down the hall if you want it taken before you go.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Down the hall, okay. Doctor, those aching legs from before, they won't come back just because I'm on the water tablet and the one white one?
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Those aches were put down to the cholesterol tablet, and that one stays stopped. If a new ache starts, ring us, don't sit on it until the two weeks are up.
